headline: A Custom Cabinetry Brand's Meta Ads Launch: 118 Leads in Month One
summary_line: PPC Guru launched a Meta Ads lead program for Lavish Artigiano, a custom cabinetry brand. In its first complete month (July 2026) the account generated 118 lead-form enquiries at $5.29 each on a $624 budget. This is an early-stage snapshot: with only one month of data live, it shows a promising start rather than an established trend.
client_context: Lavish Artigiano is a custom cabinetry and artisan millwork brand serving homeowners and renovators in Canada. Cabinetry is a considered, higher-value purchase, so the business relies on a steady stream of qualified enquiries from people planning kitchens, storage and built-in projects. Meta Ads lets the brand showcase its craftsmanship on Facebook and Instagram and capture interested homeowners' details directly through lead forms.
background: Lavish Artigiano partnered with PPC Guru to build a Meta Ads lead channel from scratch. This is a brand-new launch: PPC Guru set up a single Instant Form lead-and-calls campaign, the lead form and tracking, and began delivery in July 2026. Because only one complete month of data exists so far, this write-up is an honest first-month snapshot rather than a before-and-after case study.
analysis: The launch plan was to prove the channel efficiently before scaling. A single lead campaign kept the modest budget concentrated so the account could learn quickly against a clear signal — genuine form submissions — while showcasing the brand's cabinetry work to homeowners actively planning projects.
analysis_points: Launch one focused Instant Form campaign to capture cabinetry enquiries in-platform.
Optimize toward genuine form submissions rather than clicks or reach.
Keep the first month's budget modest while validating cost per lead.
Gather a second and third month of data before drawing trend conclusions.

timeline.what: Meta Ads launch — first complete month delivered 118 lead-form enquiries at $5.29 each on a $624 budget.
Collect additional complete months to establish a stable cost-per-lead average and a trend before scaling budget.

challenge: As a brand-new Meta Ads program, the account first has to prove that Facebook and Instagram can produce genuine, good-value enquiries for a considered purchase like custom cabinetry — before any budget is scaled. The first month's job was simply to validate cost per lead and lead volume on a modest spend.

changes.why: Captured cabinetry enquiries directly in-platform and concentrated a modest budget so the account learned quickly.
Directed spend toward people who actually submit an enquiry, not just click.
Showcased the brand's cabinetry work to attract homeowners planning kitchen and built-in projects.
Kept first-month spend modest to validate cost per lead before committing to scale.

early_stage.title: First-Month Snapshot
early_stage.intro: In its first complete month of delivery (July 2026), the account produced 118 lead-form enquiries at $5.29 each on a $624 budget, with a 2.22% click-through rate. These are encouraging launch numbers, but a single month is not yet a trend.

benchmark: This is a first-month snapshot. With only one complete month of delivery, there is no prior period to compare against and no quarterly average yet. The result is a promising start; a second and third month are needed before it can be read as a settled performance level.
lessons: Launch a new Meta channel with one focused lead campaign so a modest budget learns fast.
Optimize toward genuine form submissions, not clicks, so spend chases real project enquiries.
Lead with craft-forward creative — for considered purchases, showing the work builds trust quickly.
Validate cost per lead on a modest budget before scaling.
Give a launch a few complete months before judging it — one month is a start, not a trend.
why_it_worked: A single focused campaign concentrated a modest budget and sped up early learning.
Optimizing to form submissions kept the account chasing genuine enquiries.
Craft-forward creative resonated with homeowners planning cabinetry projects.
A controlled launch budget kept the first month low-risk while cost per lead was validated.
outcome: Lavish Artigiano's Meta Ads program is one month old. Its first complete month (July 2026) delivered 118 lead-form enquiries at $5.29 each on a $624 budget — an encouraging start for a custom cabinetry brand. Because only one month of data is live, this is a snapshot rather than a proven trend. The next step is to gather additional complete months, confirm a stable cost per lead, and then scale budget with confidence.
cta: PPC Guru helps Canadian cabinetry and renovation brands launch high-quality enquiry channels with conversion-first Meta Ads and transparent reporting.
methodology: All figures are pulled directly from the client's Meta Ads account. 'Leads' are Instant Form submissions counted by Meta's lead metric. Only one complete month of delivery (July 2026) exists, so this is reported as a first-month snapshot; status is Needs Review and confidence is Low until further months of data are available.
lead_quality: Leads are homeowner-submitted Instant Forms, giving the brand contact details to follow up on genuine cabinetry project enquiries.
